response.sql:
WITH city_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    c.location,
    COUNT(*) as count
  FROM circuits c
  JOIN races r ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
  JOIN qualifying q ON r.raceId = q.raceId
  GROUP BY c.location
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(count) as grand_total,
    COUNT(*) as num_cities
  FROM city_counts
)
SELECT 
  cc.location,
  cc.count,
  cc.count * 1.0 / t.grand_total as share,
  (cc.count * 1.0 / t.grand_total) - (1.0 / t.num_cities) as above_average
FROM city_counts cc
CROSS JOIN totals t
WHERE (cc.count * 1.0 / t.grand_total) > (1.0 / t.num_cities)
ORDER BY cc.location;

assumptions.assumption: The average share is calculated as 1 / (number of distinct cities with qualifying records), since individual shares sum to 1. This follows directly from the definition: share per city = count / total, and summing across all cities gives total / total = 1, so average = 1 / N.
